# Deadliner Glass source closure

Source: /Users/aritxonly/Codes/Android/Deadliner, base 967b7da573fdfa537b45900755ec630640d2cf80. The source checkout had local modifications; source-sha256.json records exact upstream inputs. MIT license retained in LICENSE.

Package names are mechanically changed. The selected Deadliner optics, shader order, feedback, progressive material and shadow recipes are preserved. Local patch: remove the optional official miuix-glass renderer, its preference and alternative shadow branch; retain semantic GlassSurfaceRole in GlassMaterialSpec.kt. No miuix-glass module is vendored or compiled. LOCAL_SHA256.json records shipped source files after these explicit patches.

Target: Kotlin/Compose compiler 2.4.10; Compose UI/Foundation 1.12.0; Material3 1.5.0-alpha08 (semantic theme bridge); MIUIX UI/Blur/Icons 0.9.4-rc01; Shapes 1.2.0. MIUIX core/blur remain required rendering dependencies for Deadliner Glass.

One visible primary Flutter content source is recorded into one shared LayerBackdrop: the primary FlutterImageView when Hybrid Composition is active, otherwise the Flutter view. Native chrome stays outside its source. Unsupported/custom layouts are handled by AdaptiveUI's original-component renderer.

Ordinary controls and dialogs use flutter_miuix through AdaptiveUI. No native dialog bridge or Compose modal surface is shipped. The shared GPU backdrop remains dedicated to native chrome, with no PixelCopy or CPU screenshot transport.

Top-bar integration: Android standard titles, tappable text titles, enabled/disabled icons and text/loading actions use the complete root Compose TitleBar. Text actions use the canonical SoftGlassButton and DeadlinerMiuixDefaults closure, mechanically repackaged without optical changes. A Flutter deletion footer no longer downgrades the native bar. The timetable preserves its original title layout; navigation and settings now belong to the home shell. All surfaces share one recorder; foreground/overlay images are excluded, and offstage routes stop consuming it. AdaptiveUI owns content insets and platform selection. iOS renders these same contracts with UIKit, including the native double-line timetable title.

Shared color tokens: `lib/AdaptiveUI/src/theme/deadliner_color_theme.dart` ports the pinned Deadliner color factories and component container rules recorded in source-sha256.json. Monet uses SPEC_2025 / PHONE / TonalSpot with zero contrast; the existing fixed-accent option uses Deadliner's explicit-primary SPEC_2021 path. HyperOS neutral window, card, text and divider roles override chromatic surfaces. Input containers use the canonical neutral/secondary harmonization rule. Material and flutter_miuix consume the same ThemeExtension; the complete supported role maps are transported to Compose without re-generating a palette. libmonet 1.2.0 supplies SPEC_2025 in Dart; 68 seed/mode vectors are checked against the actual pinned MaterialKolor 4.1.1 JVM implementation. iOS keeps UIKit and receives the shared onSurface/accent and explicit theme brightness.

Activity integration: an ActivityChromeLayout owns FlutterView and ComposeView as direct siblings. Flutter pointer and IME input never passes through Compose AndroidView. One gesture keeps one child target until up/cancel; Activity pause/focus loss cancels an in-flight press using the original event device/source. Window focus gates callbacks and background recording, while mounted route chrome and its last backdrop remain visible. Flutter-source invalidation schedules draw-phase GPU recording only; scroll updates transport one owner/offset pair instead of the entire theme.

The soft-glass back glyph is the user-selected `MiuixIcons.Glass.Regular.ChevronBackward` from MIUIX PR #423, pinned at 8d52b45f223d4bec9a719d3d6ca52972cc7ea5fb. It is exported as a 24dp VectorDrawable with its original 1142.9 viewport, -85.7 horizontal translation and vertical coordinate transform. No Material Symbols optical adjustment is applied. AdaptiveChromeHost mirrors it once in RTL. `miuix-back-icon-source.json` records provenance and `MIUIX_GLASS_ICONS_LICENSE` retains Apache-2.0. Only the glyph is reused; no official miuix-glass material module is added.

Home navigation reuses the complete canonical MiuixFloatingTabBar, FloatingTabMotion and FloatingNavigationShadow source closure with mechanical package renaming only. The app bridge supplies labels, MIUIX vector painters, the selected key and callbacks; the canonical bar owns optics, springs, gesture tracking and shadow. It shares the root backdrop and palette with top chrome. AdaptiveUI owns backend selection, route/keyboard visibility, accessibility and content clearance. The three tabs retain their page state, and full-screen routes stop the hidden bar consuming the backdrop. This home has no detached global action; courses expose explicit add/import entry points.

Android home tabs use the canonical Stacked layout (54dp, maximum 80dp per item) with MiuixIcons.Months, NotesFill and ContactsCircle from the pinned MIUIX icon dependency. The Activity root now owns both top and bottom Compose chrome, and dispatches one native gesture directly to the appropriate chrome bounds. Flutter publishes deduplicated geometry and semantic actions over nju/compose-navigation; no platform view is created for bottom tabs. The capsule rests at navigation padding + 2dp. The timetable viewport extends underneath it, while scroll content keeps enough trailing clearance to reveal the last row.

Focus/resume recovery explicitly ends the native Compose pointer stream using a cancel copied from the original device event, and starts a new transient navigation gesture scope. The canonical selected route, backdrop and material stay hoisted and visible. Dispatch checks current Activity resume/focus state rather than a callback's captured draw-frame flag. The emulator driver in integration_test/driver/android_home_tabs_driver.py validates interrupted presses, a completed sleep/unlock transition and exactly one subsequent tap, plus Material/Compose renderer switching.

Route animation ticks publish transformed navigation bounds, including a retained route behind a transition. Native input begins only after its Compose nodes have laid out; Flutter semantic/tap targets handle the short warm-up interval. Renderer switching on the settings route and returning to home is covered by the physical-touch emulator driver.

MIUIX dialogs fill the available phone width with 12dp side margins and a 560dp large-screen cap, honoring explicitly narrower dialog constraints. The original arbitrary form body keeps its width even when its text is short; keyboard and vertical safe-area bounds remain enforced.

The timetable publishes its optional background-derived title foreground through AdaptiveNavigationAppearance. AdaptiveUI stores it per home tab and derives the opposite Android navigation brightness with the existing seed and Monet setting. Material and Compose use that same palette; other tabs restore the app theme, and UIKit navigation retains its platform styling. Compose navigation has its own Material/MIUIX theme provider, isolated from top chrome, while continuing to share the one backdrop.

Free-time courses now use a compact Adaptive entry between the date/week header and weekday grid. The row opens the existing details flow, consumes layout space only when enabled and nonempty, and is included in fit-to-screen row sizing. It replaces the bottom floating banner and scroll-direction visibility listener.

Course category tabs reuse the complete canonical ImmersiveTextTabRow and TabRow source closure, mechanically repackaged from the recorded Deadliner checkout. They use the same root backdrop as top and bottom chrome. A separate nju/compose-tabs owner/channel prevents category and home navigation from replacing each other's callbacks. AdaptiveTabRow preserves controlled category selection across renderer changes; UIKit uses native UISegmentedControl, and original Android mode uses SegmentedButton. Hidden routes, modal overlays and keyboard presentation stop native category chrome; large text falls back to an expanding Flutter control.
